messages:
Jenna: Heads-up on Aviatrix onboarding. Peak concurrency hit ~210 this morning, p50 ~140ms, p95 ~1.2s, avg tokens/call ~900. Cost trending ~2.6x our forecast. Can we put together a preemptive performance play?
Carlos: Oof. Do we have a representative traffic slice + a few prompt examples? need to map short vs long requests.
Jenna: I grabbed 45m (09:10-09:55 UTC) and attached a short+long prompt pair. Link: https://redwood.internal/metrics/aviatrix/onboard/179555...
Samir: Quick strategy: three axes - selective quant per endpoint, lightweight distilled model for non-critical endpoints, and dynamic routing by request shape. Also add adaptive batching for bursty short ops.
Anika (Aviatrix): We care most about extraction accuracy for billing flows. Summaries can tolerate a small perf delta.
Samir: Perfect. Proposal details:
1) Endpoint tagging: label requests as "billing-extract" vs "ai-assist" via header x-req-purpose.
2) Quant profiles: billing-extract -> keep fp16; ai-assist (long summaries) -> q8_0 or q4_0 depending on eval.
3) Model swap: route ai-assist short/low-criticality to rw/distil-3b for sampling tasks. Keep billing-extract on base-7b float16.
4) Routing rule: short requests (<300 tokens) -> hosted-distil; long requests -> dedicated-large with seq-opt. Use prefix KV caching for repeated system prompts.
Carlos: Can you show a minimal routing config?
Samir: Sure snippet (JSON):
```json
{
  "match": {"account_id": "aviatrix-42"},
  "selectors": [
    {"condition": "header.x-req-purpose == 'billing-extract'", "route": {"deployment": "hosted-base-7b", "percent": 100}},
    {"condition": "meta.tokens < 300", "route": {"deployment": "hosted-distil-3b-q8", "percent": 80}},
    {"condition": "meta.tokens >= 300", "route": {"deployment": "dedicated-large", "percent": 100}}
  ],
  "fallback": "hosted-fallback"
}
```
Jenna: Ops note: we'll keep canary <= 5% for distilled swap on ai-assist, and enable A/B logging to track exact_match, f1 and hallucination_rate.
Anika (Aviatrix): 5% canary ok. Our QA will watch extraction accuracy closely for 12h.
ops-bot: Canary requested: rwctl route apply --account aviatrix-42 --file ./routes/aviatrix_preemptive.json --canary 5% (request-id: r-2026-1795551250)
Samir: Guardrails: rollback if billing-extract EM drops >1.0% absolute OR hallucination_rate increases by >0.7% OR p95 for billing-extract increases >200ms.
Jenna: I'll open CS ticket and assign owners: Carlos -> eval runs, Samir -> runbook + routing snippet, Anika QA -> manual checks.
Carlos: Kicked off eval: `rwctl eval run --account aviatrix-42 --models rw/distil-3b-q8,rw/base-7b-fp16 --prompts ./aviatrix_goldset.json --metrics latency,exact_match,f1,hallucination_rate`
ops-bot: Eval job queued (eval-id: e-2026-1795551260)
Carlos: Update: eval results done. distil-3b-q8: token cost -55% vs base-7b, p95 latency -45% on short path. Billing-extract EM change: -0.5% absolute; F1 -0.6 points. Hallucination_rate +0.2%.
Anika (Aviatrix): That's within our risk tolerance for ai-assist. Billing flows look fine. Proceed with 5% canary.
Samir: I'll publish a 1-pager + 3-step runbook: how to toggle route in Console, rwctl commands for canary bump/rollback, and the rollback thresholds. Sharing link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/aviatrix-performance-1pager
Jenna: Scheduling 30m sync tomorrow 9am PT to review telemetry after 12h QA watch. Closing loop in renewal tracker once stable.
Anika (Aviatrix): Thanks everyone. Appreciate the proactive plan and clear guardrails.
